  "findings": [
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F1",
      "proposition": "Assignment supports an awareness benefit among observed pairs: awareness rose 27.93 percentage points in the assigned arm versus 14.33 in control, an additional 13.59 points (95% CI 9.52–17.66; Holm p=1.81e-10).",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/ITT_awareness"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Supported within the prespecified primary family and observed-pair estimand.",
      "qualification": "Assigned/control paired N=960/1016, weighted N=965.21/999.79, ESS=834.41/876.62; eligible N=1400 per arm. Selection into follow-up prevents automatic interpretation as a full-cohort or target-population effect.",
      "topic_cluster": "campaign_outcomes"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F2",
      "proposition": "The study does not establish incremental consideration or reported use. Consideration rose 8.356 points assigned versus 8.364 control: contrast −0.008 points (95% CI −3.44 to 3.42; Holm p=.996). Usage rose 2.61 versus 3.59 points: contrast −0.98 (−2.70 to 0.74; Holm p=.528).",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/ITT_consideration", "analysis_results.json#/tables/ITT_usage"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "No statistically supported downstream assignment benefit; absence or equivalence is not established.",
      "qualification": "Assigned/control consideration pairs: N=966/1015, weighted N=973.61/1000.17, ESS=839.32/877.62; usage pairs: N=969/1007, weighted N=973.30/993.81, ESS=842.04/868.83. Each arm began with 1400 eligible households. Control growth cannot be assigned to a particular secular mechanism.",
      "topic_cluster": "campaign_outcomes"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F3",
      "proposition": "Attrition materially limits interpretation: 1019 assigned and 1070 control households returned, with weighted return rates of 72.38% and 75.98%. Returners had higher baseline consideration (30.13% versus 21.99%), higher digital confidence (46.34% versus 36.56%), and lower high budget pressure (33.68% versus 49.20%) than nonreturners.",
      "evidence_refs": [
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/followup_status_by_assignment",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/profile_followup_status_baseline",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/profile_assignment_baseline",
        "analysis_results.json#/tables/profile_assignment_returners"
      ],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive evidence of selective follow-up; direction and size of resulting outcome bias remain unknown.",
      "qualification": "Return-status denominators are all 1400 households per arm. Exact eligible/valid N, weighted N and ESS for all six baseline profiles are retained in attrition_audit. Arm differences also existed before attrition: consideration was 29.79% control versus 26.31% assigned, and 31.48% versus 28.76% among returners. These comparisons neither invalidate randomisation nor establish ignorable missingness.",
      "topic_cluster": "scope_and_attrition"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F4",
      "proposition": "Large recipient and recaller consideration gaps should not be sold as campaign lift. Logged recipients led nonrecipients by 19.12 points at follow-up, but already led by 19.15 at baseline. Recallers led by 37.24 points at follow-up and 32.35 at baseline.",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/OBS_receipt_log", "analysis_results.json#/tables/OBS_recall_post"],
